literal: If [one wants to] protect [oneself], protecting [against] difficult things [is necessary]; after [the ruler] suspects, reassuring [him] is difficult for anyone.
translation: If you wish to protect yourself, guard against committing grave errors or revealing secrets; once suspicion is aroused in the ruler's mind, it is impossible for anyone to reassure him.
modern: தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொள்ள விரும்பினால், அரிய தவறுகள் நேராதவாறு (அல்லது இரகசியங்களை) காக்க வேண்டும்; அரசர் சந்தேகம் கொண்ட பிறகு, அவரது ஐயத்தைப் போக்கித் தெளிவிப்பது எவருக்கும் இயலாத காரியம் ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet advises those who associate closely with rulers on how to maintain their safety. The poet emphasizes that the most crucial defense is to avoid committing serious mistakes or leaking confidential matters ('அரியவை போற்றல்'). Once a ruler begins to harbor suspicion ('கடுத்தபின்'), it becomes nearly impossible for anyone—including the accused or their allies—to clear that doubt and restore trust ('தேற்றுதல் யார்க்கும் அரிது'). Therefore, prevention through careful conduct is the only reliable safeguard.
